stem: A pie chart is drawn for the following expenditure breakdown of a firm: Raw materials Rs 180000, Labour Rs 120000, Overheads Rs 60000, Profit Rs 40000. What is the angle (in degrees) of the sector representing Labour?

per_option_rationale.rationale: 120 degrees = 120000/360000 x 360; total was mis-summed as 360000 excluding Profit, giving the wrong base.
90 degrees = 1/4 of 360; the student may have taken Labour as 1/4 of total rather than computing the actual ratio.
96 degrees = 120000/450000 x 360; the total was wrongly inflated to 450000 by double-counting one entry, an arithmetic slip in summing the four categories.

explanation: Total expenditure = 180000 + 120000 + 60000 + 40000 = 400000. Labour proportion = 120000/400000 = 3/10. Sector angle = (3/10) x 360 = 108 degrees.

explanation_sections.punchline: Labour proportion = 120/400 = 3/10; sector angle = 3/10 x 360 = 108 degrees.
explanation_sections.approach: Identify the model: pie chart sector angle = (category value / total) x 360. Step 1: sum all categories to get total 400000. Step 2: form ratio for Labour: 120000/400000 = 3/10. Step 3: multiply by 360.
explanation_sections.lesson: Always include every category in the total before computing a pie chart angle; omitting any category inflates the sector.
